From: John Taylor, Grantham

Hello Brian,

The Assembler & Disassembler are
great. Any tips to tidy up the
printing? Can we have condensed
mode in the Assembler too? In
both programs, can we have a
CHR$ 9 at the beginning of each
line so that the first 8 cols
are empty? Otherwise avoid TABS
in all print routines. Print
spaces - it's more reliable.

I am thinking of re-organising
my OUTLETs by deleting the
adverts and text items that are
no longer relevant. I shall
probably put all the Ticket
episodes on one cartridge. Can I

easily re-organise the OUTDEX or
re-write it?

One last point. I know in an
early edition someone complained
about comms material even though
there wasn't any. Why is it
avoided? If anything that is
possible on the Spectrum is not
included then OUTLET is the
poorer for it. since the
introduction of frame charges
may have drastically  cut their
time online. OUTLET should
consider these heartbroken key
thumpers. Give a needy Netter a
good home. No one wants the
8-bit hobbyist and I can never
see any of the 16-bit machines
becoming hobby machines.They are
for the people who BUY programs.

Sorry if all this doesn't hang
together properly. I have just
been through all the editions of
OUTLET and I doubt if even you
expected to do so well. OUTLET
runs to 22 cartridges and you
are only 13 months old. All the
best for Year 2!


            Regards,

              John

To John Taylor from Brian

Printer codes in JACKSOFT and
OUTSTART can be altered at the
following lines to suit the user


INTERFACE     JACKSOFT  OUTSTART

KEMPSTON       3090       9881
OPUS/I'FACE 1  3130       9887
LPRINT III     3140       9888
DISCIPLE       3150       9889
ERASE/RE-SAVE  4980/2     9980/2

When editing OUTSTART, use POKE
23606,0 : POKE 23607,60 first or
the listing will be corrupted.
Note that I already DO avoid the
use of TABs now because of the
variations in printers.

If you re-organise your OUTLET
files you may need to rename any
that have the same names.Info is
stored in OUTDEX as BASIC DATA
at line numbers proportional to
the ASCII CODE of the first 3
letters of the program name. The
line number for any name can be
calculated with the following:-

INPUT "PROGRAM NAME? ";A$

LET L=(CODE A$*26+CODE A$(2))*13
+INT(CODE A$(3)/2)-22047

PRINT L : LIST L

The program name is then entered
as string DATA at that line (in
practice I have bent the above
rule in cases of high frequency

names). Follow the DATA with a
string holding the issue number
and then numeric DATA being the
category number, e.g.:-

1028 "ARNOLD","10",13

The program "ARNOLD" being in
Issue 10 under category 13. If
you look between lines 9701 to
9750 you will see the category
names and these can be altered
or new categories added.

Sorry about the lack of comms
material in OUTLET. This is not
due to my avoiding it but simply
that I am not very knowledgeable
about it! If anyone sends in any
comms-related material I'll be
glad to put it in OUTLET!
                         - Brian

From: John Luby,  DUNS

Dear Ron/Brian,

Both the WINDOWS and TOOLBOX
utilities in No.11 were alone
worth the price of OUTLET.I wish
I wasn't such a machine-code
dyslexic -it's not as though I
haven't tried for long enough!
Incidentally, the tape copying
routine in TOOLBOX seems to be
one published in a magazine a
few years ago. I hope Mr
Mortensen is OK for copyright.

I can't be much help with your
keyboard problem. My 128 is the
'black' kind with a standard 48k
type keyboard. I had the chance
of a +2 some time ago, but a

brief inspection suggested some
problems with plugging in
Interface 1, and past experience
had taught me that the average
Spectrum can see off 2 or 3 tape
recorders during its life, so I
didn't fancy having a rarely
used recorder 'in the box'. I
can't recall any good reason why
a 48k shouldn't fit in the case,
BUT the heat sink is quite
different (so that big
transistor might have to be
moved) and the various input and
output 'holes' are in different
places. Also, the keys bear only
alphanumeric characters, and
none of the single key commands
of the 48/128k. Single-key entry
is still there of course, but
you need to remember where


everything is. Interesting idea
though! Do write it up if you
ever try it, even if it isn't
successful. Typing on the new
keyboard is much better than the
old rubber or black plastic
keys, but still isn't up to
'office' standards. And the
whole thing takes up a bit more
room than the old Spectrum.

My limited experience with the
independant add-on keyboards has
left me with the impression that
as a generality they're non too
reliable, especially where other
peripherals are used. It would
be nice to hear from anyone who
has managed to adapt one of the
many surplus keyboards around. I
tried a couple from surplus

dealers but they weren't suit-
able(many need extra electronics
to make them work)and I couldn't
afford to keep on looking until
I got it right!At least when the
black keyboards go wrong, the
membranes are cheap!

I saw an advert a couple of
years ago (can't recall the
details, though) for a set of
springs which replaced the
rubber mat between the keys and
the membrane on a Spectrum+ to
give a better feel to the keys.
Anyone know if they're still
around?

I find I do look forward to
Outboard each month. I live in
an area where it's difficult to


buy computer equipment, serious
software or magazines. The
nearest 'serious' dealer is an
Amstrad shop. I've had my
fingers burned so often with
postal services that I now
rarely order from anyone who
hasn't been recommended.

Further to your kind comments on
my programs, can I make the
following public statement to
Outlet readers via the Letters
column? Message reads:

FOR GOD'S SAKE WRITE SOMETHING!!

I've never thought of myself as
anything other than a competant
cobbler of (I hope) reasonably
useful programs, but I must blow
my own trumpet to the extent

that my cartridges are filled
mainly with FINISHED, WORKING
software, even if most of it is
of interest only to myself. My
circle of computing friends
includes people with every kind
of equipment from Spectrums to
IBM PCs and Ataris, most of
which seem to be for display
purposes only, with software
that rarely goes further than
commercial games, and some
half-hearted half-finished (and
non-working) efforts culled from
magazine listings (well I DID
have a circle of friends!). The
point of this pompous tirade is
that:
     Programming is EASY!

   Programming is INTERESTING!

Get your fingers out!

Think of a PRACTICAL application
for your Spectrum! Have you a
book/record/video/stamp
collection? Are you buying
stationery your printer could be
producing? Could your machine be
helping you with club notices/
memberships/ stationery/ advert-
ising? Don't LOOK for programs
-WRITE THEM!

Stop swapping your computer
every year for the latest model,
-keep the old one for long
enough to REALLY master it!

Don't let people tell you that
"of course you can't REALLY
program" until you've learned

machine-code, or Pascal, or
Forth, or C, or Double Dutch! Or
that you REALLY need a PROPER
machine, with 16 bit CPU and a
million megabytes! It's the idea
that counts, and you can do
wonders with good old BASIC and
just 48k! Don't be a computer
snob! GET ON WITH IT! NOW!!!

Message ends.

There now! I do feel better for
that! Better go now, or I'll
miss another issue!

Cheers,

John Luby.

P.S. Can't resist a final
grumble. Issue 11 was one of the
best yet, but is there some
secret competition for the worst
spelling? Have you been bought
out by the Grudian? Is the
apostrophe doomed to wander
aimlessly forever, leaving its
(no, NOT "it's") rightful places
to reside where it doesn't
belong? You're (no, NOT "your")
going to have to start using
your (no, NOT "you're")
dictionaries! (Now then, how big
a dictionary could we fit into a
128K? Hmmmmm....)

To John Luby from Brian

I thought I'd weeded out all the
spelling mistakes, John! I would
have been surprised to find even
one error after scouring through
but it sounds like you've found
several! I must go back and look
at Issue 11. Meanwhile, just to
get my own back, I've left the
unusual spelling of "competent"
in your letter for everyone to
gloat at and some of the liberal
comma-and-conjuction usage which
is grammatically dubious (any
clever people out there know for
sure?)
                       - Brian

From A.E.Heard,  Coventry

Hello Brian & Ron

Thanks for OUTLET No.12. I'd
like to say thank you for an
excellent magazine, though a lot
of your letters seem to be about
members' problems with Micro-
drives That is why I went for
discs. After all Microdrives are
only another type of cassette
inasmuch as the storage medium
is tape.

My present set-up consists of a
SPECTRUM+2, DISCIPLE, two 5.25
inch 80 track double-sided disc
drives and a TANDY printer-
plotter.I never have any trouble
putting programs on to disc from
tape thanks to the Disciple


button which will zap anything
on to the disc in about 4
seconds flat.

The disc drives were purchased
at a Radio Ham Rally at a very
reasonable price. Your readers
may be interested to know that
there are an increasing number
of stalls at the Rallies which
sell DISC DRIVES, COMPUTERS,
MONITORS, PRINTERS, DISCS, etc.
All at reasonable prices.

Reference Andrew Clapham's
request for a program to print
labels for cassettes. I have a
program copied from a magazine
years ago which will do this. If
you can put him in touch with me
I can let him have a copy on
cassette.

To: A.E. Heard from Brian

It's interesting to hear that
computer hardware is often sold
at Radio Ham Rallies. I presume
they are advertised in Ham Radio
magazines? (or sandwich boards?)
Anytime you know of one coming
up write in and let us know so
we can put a message in OUTLET.

I'm almost certain that Andrew
Clapham has now got a program to
print labels but Andrew, if you
would like to get in touch,write
in...
             - Brian

Trevor Wright,  Melton Mowbray

Dear Ron,

Please find enclosed a photocopy
of a letter received from Softek
yesterday. [SEE NEXT PAGE - BC]
Perhaps you would like to pass
on this rather disappointing
news to all the other OUTLET
readers. Perhaps somebody in
INDUG, the Disciple and Plus D
User group could come up with an
answer.

You inferred in OUTLETTERS 12
about not being able to find a
wordprocessor to rival Tasword
II. Well I'm using Wordmaster
from Cardex (you reviewed this
and their other desktop publish-
ing programs in an earlier

OUTLET)and I'm very,very pleased
with it.Also I've got"Typeliner"
which lets you do some real
desktop publishing. This really
looks an excellent program
although I need a bit more time
to explore its possibilities.
             Yours,
                Trevor Wright

    TEXT FROM SOFTEK LETTER:-
..Unfortunately we are unable to
help you. The "Writer" programme
was not designed to work with
that particular disc-drive.
[DISCIPLE/PLUS D]

It is rather more difficult to
make it work than it first seems
and due to relative low demand
we are not planning a version
for the disk-drive.

Dear Trevor,
I note you're getting on OK with
Wordmaster- maybe I'm too impat-
ient but I found it too compli-
cated for what I need in a word
processor. The great thing about
Tasword Two is that a lot of the
control is in Basic which makes
it easier to write your own rou-
tines to customise the program.
If anyone is still using Tasword
Two with the original Basic,
maybe we'll publish some of our
controlling Basic in OUTLET so
that readers can see what can be
done. We can't include the main
machine code program as this is,
of course, copyright, so unless
a good proportion of readers can
find a use for a new Tasword Two
Basic, it wouldn't be a sensible
excercise.           - Ron

From: Frank Lambert,  Hornchurch

Dear Ron and Brian Cavers,

The initializing for LPRINT III
in your program seems to be in-
correct-at least with my version
of LPRINT III.. [details edited
out - B.C.]

However,  a few months ago I in-
vested in a MULTIPRINT although
I haven't got it to work yet de-
spite having returned it twice!
When it is working I'll have to
patch in a further initializing
routine.

However John Luby's and Mike
Haine's contributions to Iss.
011 have given me other thoughts
on the matter. I must say I look

forward to seeing MH's program.
I wrote a basic prog. for myself
using sheet feed and reverse
drive to give "side by side"
printing. However I found that
there were variable amoounts of
memory available on different
Issues.In consequence I then had
to write in 'deletes'to gain the
extra space.

I have now come to the conclus-
ion that the best way is to go
one stage further than John Luby
suggests and have only a "USER'S
OWN" Printer/ Printer Interface
Init. and all that need be shown
are line numbers and the space
available. Hope that doesn't put
too many cats among the pigeons!

Yours sincerely, Frank Lambert.

To Frank Lambert from Brian

I presume you mean that EVERYONE
will have to MERGE in their own
printer initialization routines
in OUTLET programs?I don't think
that will be very popular! We're
checking the source of our info
about LPRINT III. Meanwhile, if
anyone IS using LPRINT III from
OUTLET successfully PLEASE WRITE
IN IMMEDIATELY as I am thinking
of replacing the option with the
suggested "User's own routine"
option. Options for Opus, I'Face
1, Kempston E and Disciple will
remain.
                - Brian

From Mark Battison

Dear Chezron,

Would Tasword 3 files be as
convenient for you as Tasword 2?
[for OUTLETTERS - B.C.]

I suspect a mistake in your
feature on microdrives from
Applied Technology in Issue 11.
It was said that the ribbon
connector was to be used between
microdrives and not the small
double-edged connector. Have I
misread the article or is there
a mistake?

What is the Cardex package you
mentioned and where can it be
obtained from?

Several issues ago, you gave the
readership  numbers  of  various
"paper" computer magazines.I was
surprised you did not add OUTLET
to the list. I would be quite
interested to know how many
people subscribe to OUTLET.

I managed to spot the deliberate
error in VidList.Try listing by
title if you have not found it.

By the way, my local branch of
John Menzies is selling Micro-
drive cartridges at `1.45 each.

Bye for now,

Mark Battison

To: Mark Battison from Brian


No, Tasword 3 files are NOT as
convenient for us as Tasword 2
files.I may take up your idea of
a Tas 3 to Tas 2 utility!

The awful error in the DRIVECHAT
article on microdrives is my own
fault!Somehow, when typing it in
from the original I thought it
was wrong and altered it! I just
can't believe it now but it must
have been my fault. The original
said ensure you use the ribbon
connector between the first
microdrive AND THE SPECTRUM! I
repent in sackcloth and ashes
with nobs on.

While I'm at it, the VIDLIST
error is also my fault! I had to
extensively re-write VIDLIST to
recover enough memory to include
the printer options and the
BASIC that links with OUTLET. To
correct the fault, edit out line
3030 and add one space to the
long string of spaces after the
PRINT #S;"... etc. which is used
to tabulate.

The Cardex package is a word-
processor called WORD-MASTER at
`14.95 and other graphics and
desk-top publishing utilities.It
is reviewed in the CHECKOUT in
Issue 8 and obtainable from:
CARDEX, 3 Barton Street, Barrow-
in-Furness, Cumbria LA14 2EP
(Phone: 0229 36957)

Our readership is still very
tiny - only around 150 regulars
I think! You can appreciate how
demoralizing this can be after
striving for a year. The problem
is that we have no capital to
invest in promotion to speak of
and, even though we think there
is a potential market of many
thousands, unless we can reach
them we can't improve our sales.
We have written many times to
CRASH magazine and sent them
review copies but they just
ignore us! It seems unless you
are a mega software house sell-
ing games they don't want to
know! Now if a few dozen readers
wrote to them and complained...

                     - Brian.

From: Mr. E.M. Duffield

Dear Ron & Brian,

Reference to Mr Goldsworthy's
query,I've no experience of the
Centronics form of transmission.
I agree with Brian's remarks and
can only suggest that the cable
is at fault.I was given a centr-
onics cable with my Wafadrive
but as it was of no use to me I
cut it up for other uses.However
I do remember that three or four
wires were crossed over and the
26 way IDC plug had a label with
TOP on it. Now there are many
different kinds of plug but this
one is about the only one that
does not have a method of locat-
ion. The Manual says it could be


harmful to connect the unit
wrongly and as the cables are
quite expensive I think Mr Gold-
sworthy should go back to his
supplier. Brother who make the
HR5 and the EP44 usually give a
separate booklet on how to make
up your own cables and should be
quite helpful.

If Mr. Goldsworthy's trouble is
really RS232 then I reversed the
handshake lines:

        RTS A4 TO RTS A3
        CTS A3 TO CTS A4

I have been using JACKSOFT quite
a lot over the past few days and
although I dislike Assemblers
this one has all the good points

and none of the bad that all
others have.

Brian suggests taking a printout
of the instructions. I replied
Interface 1 to the Menu and
changed the Baud rate to 1200
but all I got was'uU'and another
time'UU' and then something made
the printer lock up, but having
had previous experience of this
I went through the printer reset
button procedure and all was
well again.

I believe the baud rate was
still too high. However, I got
back to BASIC and peeked 23747.
The result was 10 and not 110 as
it should be for 1200 baud. Any-
how it was worth making a print-
ed copy.

I like Brian's machine code
lessons and hope he gets suffic-
ient support to continue the
series.

          E.M.Duffield

In a separate letter Mr.Duffield
says he would like to make it
clear that any hardware dabbling
undertaken by readers should be
at their own risk as the most
important factor is experience.

With reference to DRIVECHAT
later in this issue,he also says
that he DID get another OPD unit
from John Bull& Co.but one drive
was faulty(and was labelled so!)
thus it could be they are sold
cheaply on the understanding
that there may be faults.Anyway,
their address is:

      J & N BULL ELECTRICAL
      250 PORTLAND ROAD,
      HOVE, BRIGHTON
      SUSSEX BN3 5QT

To Mr. E.M. Duffield from Brian

Since reading Mr. Goldsworthy's
letter I've discovered that BOTH
the WAFADRIVE and his printer
support EITHER centronics OR
RS232 so it must be worth double
checking that both are adjusted
correctly, ie. the printer dip
switches are set correctly and
the WAFADRIVE initialized as it
should be.

Regarding the JACKSOFT print-out
I must say that the FORMAT is an
ordinary BASIC FORMAT command so
it can't really be a fault with
the program. Probably just a
tempory mains surge or hiccup?

                   - Brian

From Brian Gaff

I have an early Swift 2 now it
looks good for 48K owners. The
128K does not like it though
(surprise huh?). It is about the
size of the old FOX interface
boxes - in fact it could be one!
You can turn the joystick off
too from s/ware. It has hardware
to trap the CLOSE # error that
affected the old one and emulate
the write enable direct hardware
call. The address you put for
SIXWORD is wrong.The new address
is:-
          SIXWORD LTD.
       24 Chatsworth Close
       Catisfield, Fareham
       Hampshire  PO15 5LS
        Tel: 0243 771689

Regarding the index,I think that
the monthly approach is better
as we can get into the habit of
updating it.Once a year would be
no good as most of the time I
need a program it's month's old.

I have been running OUTLET on my
+3 in +3 mode. This should be no
problem as long as you  stay  in
48K mode. Multiface 1  works  as
well as the VTX.

On the subject of the chap with
the 4K microdrive, I would guess
that the internal adjustment of
the head has moved in transit,
possibly the motor too. The
design is not exactly robust! If
he wants I will have a look at
it for him - no charge except
for carriage costs.

The keyboard on the 128K is
generally not that robust. It is
the same as the + of course. I
get through a membrane every 18
months or so. I wonder if a +2
keyboard could be used?

Printers: I have a Brother M1009
and an Alphacom. I use I'Face 1
or the Swift version. I also use
the +3's Centronics port but of
course, not in 48K mode!

                Brian Gaff

Many thanks, Brian. Er... About
the +3. Are you saying you have
OUTLET loading and running from
the +3 disk with no problems!!??

                Brian Cavers.

### От Brian для John Taylor

Коды принтера в JACKSOFT и OUTSTART можно изменить под свои нужды в следующих строках:

```text
ИНТЕРФЕЙС     JACKSOFT  OUTSTART

KEMPSTON       3090       9881
OPUS/I'FACE 1  3130       9887
LPRINT III     3140       9888
DISCIPLE       3150       9889
ERASE/RE-SAVE  4980/2     9980/2
```

При редактировании OUTSTART сначала выполните `POKE 23606,0 : POKE 23607,60`, иначе листинг испортится. Заметь, что сейчас я ДЕЙСТВИТЕЛЬНО избегаю использования TAB из-за различий между принтерами.

Если ты будешь реорганизовывать файлы OUTLET, возможно, придётся переименовать те из них, у которых совпадают имена. Информация хранится в OUTDEX в виде данных BASIC DATA в номерах строк, пропорциональных коду ASCII первых 3 букв названия программы. Номер строки для любого имени можно рассчитать следующим образом:

```text
INPUT "PROGRAM NAME? ";A$

LET L=(CODE A$*26+CODE A$(2))*13+INT(CODE A$(3)/2)-22047

PRINT L : LIST L
```

Затем имя программы вводится как строковые DATA в этой строке (на практике я иногда отступал от этого правила в случаях слишком часто встречающихся названий). После имени программы укажите строку с номером выпуска, а затем числовые DATA — номер категории, например:

```text
1028 "ARNOLD","10",13
```

Программа «ARNOLD» находится в выпуске 10 под категорией 13. Если вы посмотрите строки с 9701 по 9750, то увидите названия категорий — их можно изменять или добавлять новые.

Прошу прощения за отсутствие материалов по связи (comms) в OUTLET. Дело вовсе не в том, что я избегаю этой темы, а просто в том, что я в ней не очень разбираюсь! Если кто-нибудь пришлёт материалы, связанные с модемной связью, я с радостью опубликую их в OUTLET!  
— Brian

### От: John Luby, DUNS

Дорогие Ron и Brian,

Кстати, процедура копирования ленты в TOOLBOX подозрительно напоминает ту, что была опубликована в одном журнале пару лет назад. Надеюсь, у мистера Mortensen всё в порядке с авторскими правами.

Вряд ли я смогу сильно помочь с вашей проблемой с клавиатурой. У меня «чёрная» модель 128 со стандартной клавиатурой типа 48k. Некоторое время назад у меня была возможность взять +2, но беглый осмотр показал проблемы с подключением Interface 1, а прошлый опыт научил меня, что среднестатистический Spectrum за свою жизнь успевает пережить 2–3 магнитофона. Поэтому перспектива иметь редко используемый магнитофон «в одном корпусе» меня не прельщала. Я не вижу веских причин, почему плата 48k не должна поместиться в корпус, НО радиатор там совершенно другой (так что тот большой транзистор, возможно, придётся перенести), да и отверстия для входов и выходов находятся в других местах. Кроме того, на клавишах нанесены только буквенно-цифровые символы и нет команд, вводимых одним нажатием, как на 48/128k. Однокнопочный ввод, конечно, никуда не делся, но придётся помнить наизусть, где что находится. И всё же идея интересная! Обязательно напишите об этом, если попробуете, даже если ничего не выйдет. Набирать текст на новой клавиатуре гораздо приятнее, чем на старых резиновых или чёрных пластиковых клавишах, но до «офисного» стандарта она всё равно не дотягивает. Да и места вся эта конструкция занимает побольше, чем старый Spectrum.

Мой скромный опыт работы с отдельными внешними клавиатурами оставил впечатление, что в массе своей они не слишком надёжны, особенно когда используются другие периферийные устройства. Было бы здорово услышать кого-нибудь, кому удалось приспособить одну из многочисленных клавиатур с распродаж неликвидов. Я пробовал пару штук из таких магазинов, но они не подошли (многим требуется дополнительная электроника, чтобы заставить их работать), а продолжать поиски методом проб и ошибок мне было не по карману! По крайней мере, когда ломаются чёрные клавиатуры, мембраны для них стоят дёшево!

Пару лет назад я видел рекламу (деталей уже не помню) набора пружин, которые устанавливались вместо резинового коврика между клавишами и мембраной на Spectrum+, чтобы улучшить тактильные ощущения. Кто-нибудь знает, продаются ли они ещё?

Я с нетерпением жду Outboard каждый месяц. Я живу в районе, где трудно купить компьютерное «железо», серьёзный софт или журналы. Ближайший «серьёзный» дилер — магазин Amstrad. Я уже столько раз обжигался на почтовых службах, что теперь редко заказываю у кого-то без рекомендации.

Возвращаясь к вашим добрым отзывам о моих программах: могу ли я сделать следующее публичное заявление читателям Outlet через колонку писем? Текст сообщения:

РАДИ БОГА, НАПИШИТЕ ХОТЬ ЧТО-НИБУДЬ!!

Я никогда не считал себя кем-то большим, чем посредственным клепателем (надеюсь) умеренно полезных программ, но не могу не похвастаться тем, что мои картриджи забиты преимущественно ГОТОВЫМ, РАБОТАЮЩИМ софтом, пусть даже большая его часть интересна только мне самому. В круг моих друзей-компьютерщиков входят владельцы всевозможного оборудования — от Spectrum до IBM PC и Atari. Однако большая часть этой техники, похоже, стоит исключительно для красоты, а софт редко выходит за рамки коммерческих игр и невнятных недоделанных (и неработающих) попыток набрать листинги из журналов (ну ладно, БЫЛ у меня когда-то круг друзей!). Не позволяйте людям вешать вам лапшу на уши о том, что «вы, конечно же, не умеете НА САМОМ ДЕЛЕ программировать», пока не выучите машинный код, Паскаль, Форт, Си или марсианский язык!
